desc: AI scene: japandi home office, blank-insert frame (art cover-fits the insert)
prompt: Photorealistic japandi home office interior featuring one vertical piece of wall art (3:4 ratio). Realistic textures, subtle decor and authentic lived-in detail. Lighting is natural daylight from a window, falling in one consistent direction. Time and season: late afternoon, around 5 pm, on a fresh spring day, the sun bright and clean with a light, slightly cool warmth. The window is off to one side of the art wall, so the light rakes across the wall from that side and shows its texture. Light style: direct window light with soft-edged, clearly visible shadows: warm sunlit patches with gently feathered edges on the floor and the wall, calm and inviting. Photographer and stylist: a bright Scandinavian interiors catalogue: pale, airy and uncluttered, one green plant, crisp tidy styling. Display: the artwork hangs alone on a calm stretch of wall with generous space around it. Camera: a 3/4 corner view from the right, about 30 degrees off square, so the depth of the room reads clearly. Camera height: standing eye height, about 160 cm. Framing: a medium shot of the art wall and what sits below it, the artwork about a third of the image height. Lens: a natural 35-50 mm view with true proportions. Foreground: the edge of a rug or a folded throw runs along the bottom of the picture, well below the frame. Focus: everything sharp from front to back, the artwork crisp. Composition: the artwork on the right third of the picture, the room opening to the left. Walls: a light warm greige. The wall is smooth painted plaster. Floor: honey-toned wood planks. Furniture: rattan and cane mixed with wood. Whatever the light, the artwork itself hangs in calm, even light: sun patches, shadows and any blind or leaf pattern land on the floor and on the wall around the frame, while the whole printed area stays one flat, evenly lit tone; the frame, the mat or canvas edge and the wall each stay clearly distinct, with crisp, unbroken outlines. The whole frame sits inside the picture with clear wall on all four sides; nothing in front of it overlaps any part of the frame. The artwork face is flat, upright and in sharp focus, and the frame stands out clearly from the wall in tone. The picture is a vertical (portrait) photograph with the artwork as its clear focal point. Only one piece of wall art, no other picture frames, posters or mirrors. The artwork's printed area is a single flat, plain, empty, blank onion-skin orange (a pale peachy-orange, roughly RGB 250, 215, 170) surface with a dead-matte, non-reflective finish like unglazed matte card: one even tone from edge to edge, evenly lit across its whole face, glare-free and free of hot spots, so it reads as one clean flat colour. The orange appears only on the front face of the printed area. Its matte surface absorbs the light, so every surface next to it keeps its own natural colour in the room's own light: the frame and its inner edge stay their wood, metal or paint colour, any gap stays a natural neutral shadow, and the wall stays the wall colour. The artwork is a thick stretched gallery canvas, 1.5 to 2 inches (4-5 cm) deep, mounted inside a thin NATURAL LIGHT WOOD floater frame (floating frame), a warm natural wood colour, never black or dark. Only the FRONT FACE of the canvas is orange. The canvas side edges (the wrap around the stretcher bars) are plain clean WHITE, clearly a different tone from the orange face, so the front face ends in one crisp straight line where the white side edge begins; the side edges are never orange, never black: they stay clean white in the light and neutral grey where they turn into shadow. The canvas sits inset inside the frame with a narrow even visible gap of about 0.5 cm between the canvas edge and the frame's inner lip; the gap holds a natural soft shadow in the neutral tones of the wood, lighter than black, so the pale wood frame, the thin gap, the white canvas side edge and the orange face are clearly separate bands. The piece stands off the wall by the canvas depth and casts a natural shadow on the wall that follows the room's light direction. The floater frame's natural wood is a mid-tone honey oak, clearly darker than the wall, so its outer edge stands out crisply against the wall. The side edge facing the camera shows the canvas depth. No people, no faces, no hands, no pets. No lamps unless the room clearly needs one; only props a real person would leave there. Wall paneling or wainscoting only if the room style calls for it (elegant or traditional rooms); if used, either keep it below waist height and fully below the frame, or make the panels larger than the frame with the frame hanging centred inside one panel, with clear wall space on every side; the frame never touches or overlaps any molding, rail or panel edge.
